claims.facts_text: EmbeddingGemma-2 frame heads pooled over every 0.5 s frame: AUROC 0.808 (0.70-0.86)

claims.protocol: frame head = logistic (C=1) trained on 8000 AI-labelled factory frames (gemini-2.5-flash, NOT human); applied to every 0.5 s frame of each window (3005 frames, mean 20.03/window); pooled per window into 12 features (mean/max/p25/p75/frac>0.5/var x {active_labor,hands_ok}); window logistic, outer leave-one-clip-out, inner-LOCO C in {0.01,0.1,1,10}, class_weight=balanced; clip bootstrap n=2000 seed=0

protocol_ambiguities: FACTS 17:40 quotes 0.808 and 17:50 quotes 0.79 for the same nominal 'frame heads pooled over every 0.5 s frame' protocol; they are the 8k-heads and 10k-heads runs respectively. Neither line names the training set. Both reproduce from their own artifact.
The 0.816 'EG2 human-only head' is not a frame head: it is a logistic on the 768-d window-mean EG2 embedding, uses no AI frame labels, and is identical in the 8k and 10k runs.

The perpixel trio (conv1d 0.782 / HGB 0.758 / physics 0.715) is computed on the 137-window activity subset (100 good vs 37 bad), not on all 150 windows, although FACTS's block header says 'on the 150 human windows'. compare.json's own protocol line also says '150 windows'.

Published clip bootstrap in analyze_transfer.py resamples the 7 clips but then takes the UNION of their windows (np.isin), i.e. repeated clips are not duplicated. This gives slightly narrower intervals than a proper cluster bootstrap: human-only 0.8164 published [0.710,0.892] vs proper [0.678,0.902]; pooled 0.7914 [0.688,0.863] vs [0.655,0.863]. The perpixel scripts do duplicate windows (proper variant).
'Intervals touching 0.5' for the harness arms is true for 7 of the 8 n=150 arms; A-full's CI [0.509,0.641] excludes 0.5.
findings: The producing artifacts for the EG2 frame-head claims are NOT on origin/main: eval/results/frames10k/ exists only on the unmerged origin/feat/frames10k branch (head file blobs listed above). FACTS.md itself is also absent from origin/main (pod bundle only).

The exact GPU multi-head 'work' head value 0.41 is not reproducible from the committed state on CPU or GPU (0.494/0.516); the 'no transfer' conclusion is reproduced. The producer reads its training features from another worker's live worktree path, and that file was regenerated after the run (blob 52ac9c99 -> f91385e2); re-running with the older blob also gives 0.494, so the exact value is not pinned by any committed input.

frames-spectral's own window transfer (full_pipeline 0.7472 [0.6107,0.8241], n=150, blob a0694eb8) is a separate arm not covered by the harness range in FACTS 17:50; the registry backfill (L1.28) claims those window numbers were 'not extracted', but the committed JSON contains them.
The 0.60 EG2 harness head in the base FACTS section is stale (final n=150 artifact: 0.496); it matches only the superseded 79-window partial (0.596).
